Formula: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
Exact Expression: f'(c) = \frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}
Definitions: States that for any continuous and differentiable curve, there exists at least one point where the tangent is parallel to the secant connecting the endpoints.
Derivation/Reference: Derived from Rolle's theorem applied to auxiliary function h(x) = f(x) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)](x-a); Joseph-Louis Lagrange (1797)
Example: f(x) = x^2 on [0, 2] -> f'(c) = (4 - 0)/2 = 2 -> 2c = 2 -> c = 1 in (0, 2)
Domain: real_analysis
Assumptions: f is continuous on [a, b]; f is differentiable on (a, b)
Common Errors: Applying to discontinuous functions or functions non-differentiable at cusps
subject: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
